description: Heteronym substrate — 13 heteronyms (twelve Dodecad positions + Feist/LOGOS* standing outside; Lee Sharks/MANUS as human bearer; Viola Arquette Adjacent) with frame-based rotating-outside architecture, Sep 2025 preservation, v1.1 canonical reconciliation, and Mandala Oracle avatar assets.
structural_principle: The heteronym set comprises twelve Dodecad positions plus Feist/LOGOS* as the archive-default outside. Different frames rotate different figures to the outside position: Sep 2025 Logotic Science places Nobel Glas outside; v1.1 Constitutional Registry places Lee Sharks (MANUS) outside; the archive-default LOGOS frame places Feist outside. See frames.jsonl.

files.name: crosswalk.json
files.description: The heteronym dataset joined to the lexical minting registry, the concept map, the wiki and the citation graph — on the CREATOR FIELD only, so 'names X' and 'is by X' stay distinct. Carries position-level citation degrees, minted-term counts and concept membership for all twelve.

files.name: index.json
files.description: The twelve positions as an addressable set: person_id, name, canonical surface, records on surface, and whether every linked record was read end to end.

files.name: dodecad-graph.svg
files.description: The Dodecad as a citation network. Node radius is citation in-degree, edge weight is position-level citation count, ring ranked by in-degree. Edges below weight 12 omitted and the figure says so. Uses currentColor, so it inherits any surface's palette.

files.name: citation-field.svg
files.description: Every citation edge in the archive: 9,136 chords among 1,447 deposits, nothing filtered. Chord curvature is set by endpoint distance, so chords crossing the centre are late work citing early work.

files.name: lexical-field.svg
files.description: All 12,073 minted terms as motes, each placed in the sector of the position that authored its source deposit. Radius and jitter are a SHA of the term, so the same corpus always paints the same canvas. 5,056 in a voice; 7,017 in the ground.

files.name: capture-field.svg
files.description: 261 dated capture-registry entries by date across twelve section bands. Larger motes are phrase-matched queries — the stricter test. Frameworks carries 122 of 266.

resources.principle: The dataset is the canonical asset host for everything the /who/ surfaces need — not avatars alone. A satellite references these paths rather than copying the file, so one asset serves the fleet and there is one thing to keep current. img-src on satellite CSPs must admit alexanarch for this to work.

layout.avatars/{120,240}/{slug}.webp: heteronym portraits, both sizes declared per slug
layout.resources/institutions/{slug}.webp: institution charter plates, derived at 600px WebP q82
layout.resources/journals/{slug}.webp: journal covers, as print covers rather than CSS renderings

resources.derivation: Source images are frequently multi-megabyte. Derivatives are generated at 600px WebP quality 82 — the IDP charter plate went 1.8 MB PNG to 52 KB with no visible loss. Blogger /a/-form URLs honour an =s600 suffix; /b/-form URLs ignore every resize suffix and return identical bytes, so test per URL rather than assuming.

generators.lexical-field.svg: in-session generator, deterministic on term SHA

note: The four SVG fields are DERIVED, not composed: each is a projection of the archive's own data, so disagreement with a figure is disagreement with the corpus rather than with its renderer. All are deterministic — the same corpus always paints the same picture, and a change in an image means a change in the archive. Deposited under tether #1448 · AXN:05D9.ARCHIVAL.🍄🔎💡🝊🔙🏗️.
